5. A fixed stationary physical output is not a free replacement for a release basin

I checked another possible bypass: force the writer to output one fixed thermal encoding with arbitrarily small full-state error, then invoke equilibrium retention directly.

For a positive commuting stabilizer Hamiltonian, a nonidentity check  $S$  has thermal expectation

 $m_\beta\ge\tanh(\beta J_S)>0.$ Compare two legal primitive-fault adversaries under the same always-on bath:

No additional primitive replacement.

A Pauli  $P$  anticommuting with  $S$ , appended with probability  $p$  at the selected final memory operation.

At that boundary, the two outputs are  $\rho$  and
 $(1-p)\rho+pP\rho P$ . Their check expectations are  $x$  and  $(1-2p)x$ .

If both outputs must lie within trace norm  $\delta$  of the same thermal target, then, for  $0<p\le1/2$ ,

 $m_\beta-\delta
\le
(1-2p)(m_\beta+\delta),$ hence

 $\boxed{\delta\ge\frac{p\,m_\beta}{1-p}.}$ Pre-biasing the unfaulted writer does not remove this floor.

The boundary qualification is essential: no later corrective physical evolution is included. An added relaxation stage would need its own quantum-retention proof and costs. This is a full physical-state limitation; the one-site Pauli can still be logically correctable.

The thermal-phase theorem does not automatically repair this mismatch. Its memory statement requires a reference state annihilated term by term by the generator, together with the stated local-reversibility and range conditions.
